title: AeroCausal: Wind-Aware Causal Attribution of Agricultural Biomass Burning to Atmospheric PM2.5 Pollution
abstract: A proposed environmental data science investigation examining the contribution of upwind agricultural fire activity to downstream PM2.5 concentrations in Northern India. The research will integrate satellite fire observations, ground-level pollution measurements and meteorological reanalysis while explicitly evaluating causal identification assumptions, confounding and statistical uncertainty.
content:
## Research Motivation

Predictive air pollution models can estimate future pollutant concentrations but cannot independently establish causal relationships between emission sources and observed pollution. AeroCausal extends the environmental research trajectory established through ECOSIMULATE and Veridian from simulation and prediction toward causal inference.

## Primary Research Question

Under explicitly stated causal identification assumptions, what is the estimated contribution of upwind agricultural fire activity to downstream PM2.5 concentrations at selected Northern Indian monitoring locations?

## Proposed Methodology

- Integrate historical fire detections, ground-level pollution observations and meteorological variables.
- Establish temporal and spatial alignment across datasets.
- Construct wind-aware fire exposure measures.
- Investigate distributed-lag regression and fixed-effects baselines.
- Formulate causal directed acyclic graphs and identify potential confounders.
- Evaluate Double Machine Learning and alternative causal estimation approaches where justified.
- Perform robustness checks, placebo tests and sensitivity analysis.

## Candidate Datasets

NASA FIRMS, CPCB historical air quality observations, India Air Quality Database and ERA5 meteorological reanalysis. Dataset overlap, licensing, missingness and causal suitability remain subject to investigation.

## Proposed Technology Stack

Python, DuckDB, Polars, xarray, SciPy, statsmodels, DoWhy, EconML and Plotly.

## Evaluation Strategy

Estimated effect sizes, uncertainty intervals, temporal robustness, station-level heterogeneity and sensitivity to alternative exposure definitions and confounding assumptions. Address spatial and temporal dependence, exposure measurement error and interference between locations.

## Scientific Limitations

Active fire detections do not automatically establish agricultural burning. Advanced machine learning does not independently eliminate confounding. If causal identification cannot be justified, the study will report conditional associations instead.

## Current Status

Research proposal established. Development, data acquisition and experimental evaluation have not started.
